spec.difficultyPlan: Five recall, seven simple-use, five application and three challenge questions.
misconceptions: Every old object supplies a complete account without interpretation.

distractorMisconceptions.Oral tradition: Oral tradition passes knowledge by spoken accounts across generations. Here the clue points to Archaeology.
distractorMisconceptions.Contemporary diary: A diary written by a witness close to the event can serve as primary evidence about that person's experience. Here the clue points to Archaeology.

distractorMisconceptions.Numismatics: Numismatics examines coins and related evidence, such as their markings. Here the clue points to Contemporary diary.

distractorMisconceptions.Fill in the year from the coin's colour: Uses colour to guess an unreadable year. Record what can be seen first. A symbol is visible evidence, while an unreadable date remains unknown.

distractorMisconceptions.Write today's year as the year it was ma: Confuses the observation date with the date of production. Record what can be seen first. A symbol is visible evidence, while an unreadable date remains unknown.

distractorMisconceptions.Only the village where the book is kept: Records where a book is kept instead of how a story travelled. Oral tradition follows the passing on of an account. The people in that chain help us understand its source.
